(i) current growth data cannot rule out models with incorrect background cosmology, but (ii) future growth data can rule out incorrect models with a constant growth index if the background cosmology is known.
the redshift parameterization of the linear growth function can provide significant constraints on the underlying gravity model and rule out incorrect cosmologies.

the growth index parameterizations discussed in this paper are a powerful tool in the analysis of future growth data and can significantly rule out incorrect models, when the correct background is assumed.
the redshift parameterization is the best way to use the growth data in the near future, and that the constant index should be used with caution.

the redshift parameterization of growth index can be used to put significant constraints from future observations.

the growth index is not constant over all redshifts, and therefore it should be used in a parameterization that accounts for the redshift dependence of the growth function.
the redshift parameterization of the linear growth function is an efficient and robust tool for future data analysis.
